entry.title: Book Discussion | ‘A Moving Line’: Evolving Identities in Comics and Graphic Narratives
entry.summary:
Join us for this book discussion on 31st of October, Saturday at 6:00 PM at Champaca Bookstore, Vasanth Nagar.

More
entry.content:
Join us for the book discussion of A Moving Line, a celebration of India’s rich history of visual storytelling. Comic creator and visual artists Rahil Mohsin and Mia Jose will be in conversation with designer Kriti Monga to reflect on how storytelling in graphic narratives have evolved over centuries and the many nuances and developments in it. 

This will be followed by an interactive Q&A with the audience.

Here are the details:

Date: 31st October 2026, Sunday

Time: 6:00 PM (seating begins at 5:45 PM)

Venue: Champaca Bookstore, Vasanth Nagar

RSVP here to register.

About the book: 

Stories, whether written or drawn, are always moving, reshaped by every generation that inherits and retells them. India has a long and rich history of visual storytelling, from temple walls and painted scrolls to comics, graphic novels and webcomics. Published by the Museum of Art and Photography, A Moving Line traces this history, revealing unexpected connections between works that are rarely considered together.

The eight essays and eleven graphic narratives in this collection range from the timeless to the future-forward. Bringing together contributions by scholars, practitioners and artists, this book explores the many nuances and developments in sequential storytelling.

A Moving Line celebrates a medium that has always been, and continues to be, inherently visual.

Meet the speakers:

Rahil Mohsin is a Bengaluru-based comic creator and co-founder of Hallubol, the world’s first bilingual Dakhni-English comic series, created alongside children’s book creator Alankrita Amaya. His portfolio includes work with Scout Comics, Comixense, Pratham Books, Sufi Comics, and Room to Read. Inspired by the everyday lives of working-class Muslim communities, his work explores the Dakhni language, folklore, culture, and food traditions of South India through graphic narratives rooted in multilingual realities. His stories often blend humour, memory, and voices rarely seen in contemporary comics.

Mia Jose (she/they) is a trans visual artist, art director, researcher and devourer of all things camp and horror. After transitioning from an active legal practice, she now uses graphic narratives to probe questions of gender, inheritance and embodiment, informed by her identity and roots in Kerala. Her creative practice is tied to her research on visual narrative traditions in India, and she is especially interested in the emergence of comics as vehicles for queer and marginalised voices. Having published several comics of her own, she is currently splitting her time between a short comic on mental health through monsters and folklore, and a graphic novel exploring masculinity and insecurity in the context of her hometown.

Meet the moderator:

Kriti Monga brings over two decades of design experience to her multi-disciplinary practice, blending artistic expression, strategic design, and hands-on craftsmanship. The founder-director of the acclaimed Turmeric Design, her work spans brand building, book design, visual art, illustration, and mentorship. She also teaches professional design and typography programs globally.

entry.title: Brunch & Books for Kids: Read-Aloud of ‘Manvinder’s Medu Vada’
entry.summary:
Bring your little one for a brunch and read-aloud session on 10th of October, Saturday at 11:00 AM at Champaca Bookstore, Indiranagar.

More
entry.content:
Crispy, golden-brown, fluffy and white . . . who will make the perfect medu vadas for Manvinder?

Come, join us for a yummy brunch for your little one and you, followed by a read-aloud session of Manvinder’s Medu Vada, written by Riddhi Maniar Doda and illustrated by Vinayak Sharma. The read-aloud session, conducted by SkilLit Readers, will be followed by a clay modeling activity where kids will make a food item they would like to eat. 

Here are the details:

Date: 10th October 2026, Saturday

Time: 11:00 AM to 12:30 PM 

Venue: Champaca Bookstore, Indiranagar

Age group: 4-7 years

RSVP here to register.

The brunch menu curated by Copper + Cloves includes:

  • Banana bread
  • Crackers with Hummus
  • Baguettes (untoasted) with peanut butter
  • Fruit bowl

The ticket price includes brunch for 1 child and 1 adult. 

About the book:

It is Manvinder’s first time eating a Medu vada in Bengaluru, and lo, behold, he is instantly hooked to the fluffy, crunchy ball of goodness! Manvinder refuses to eat anything else and the whole family leaves no stone unturned trying to recreate the Medu vada. Written by Riddhi Maniar Doda, Manvinder's Medu Vada is all about that hilarious struggle. 

About SkillLit Readers:

SkilLit Readers is a story-led skills lab that uses books as launchpads to build independent thought and creative expression. They run book exploration programs that enable participants to think critically and connect with stories and their lives meaningfully. They strongly believe that reading is more than decoding the page and we use a range of experiential tools to bring books and stories to life.

entry.title: Lost & Found: A Book Club at Champaca
entry.summary:
Join us for this in-person book club at Champaca Bookstore, Indiranagar.

More
entry.content:
Lost & Found is an in-person book club at Champaca Bookstore, Indiranagar. It will be held once a month in October and November and will follow a single theme across two books: the idea of how literature tells the story of language, belief, and people caught mid-transition—both in English, mediated by a translator.

This series is a direct response to something we’ve been hearing often at Champaca, that readers want to spend more time with a book and to talk about it with others. Lost & Found offers a simple structure to do exactly that: read, meet, and discuss!

How the sessions work

  • Two in-person sessions, once in October and once in November

  • Each session focuses on one book from the reading list

  • Conversations are guided by open-ended prompts

  • Space for both quiet reflection and group discussion

  • A smaller group for closer, more comfortable conversations

Between sessions, participants will stay connected through an email or WhatsApp group, with reading prompts and gentle reminders.

Here are the details:

Format: In-person book club
Two sessions, once in October and once in November

Venue: Champaca Bookstore, Indiranagar

Duration: 90 minutes per session

Fee for the membership of full three-part series: INR 1999
Includes a Champaca book voucher worth INR 999, which can be used to pick up both the book club titles from our shelves, along with a Champaca notebook!

Register Here

Reading list:

October: The Gods are Leaving by D.B. Mokashi, translated from Marathi by Shanta Gokhale

November: Spontaneous Acts by Yoko Tawada, translated from German by Susan Bernofsky

Bonus: Herbarium by Sonia Rafeek, translated from Malayalam by Ministhy S.

Who is this for?

  • Regular readers looking for structured discussion
  • Readers returning to books after a break
  • Anyone who wants a small, welcoming reading group
  • Open to adults and young adults (above 16 years)
  • Someone interested in bookstores and their peculiarities 

    Seats are limited, so please register to join!

entry.title: Workshop | Cityscapes: A 2-Day Flash Fiction Writing Workshop with Cities in Fiction
entry.summary:
Join us for this workshop on 26th and 27th of September at 11:00 AM at Champaca Bookstore, Vasanth Nagar

More
entry.content:
Ever thought of turning your daily city encounters into writing ideas?

What did you notice today? A strange cloud? A burst of bougainvillea against a concrete wall? A fragment of a conversation overheard? Or perhaps, a child eating jalebies at the photocopy shop? Be it for work, study, or leisure: every time we step out of the house—through people and places—we plunge right into a labyrinth of stories. Sometimes we notice, and sometimes we just pass by them.

In this two-day workshop with Cities of Fiction, we will explore how cities—full of everyday enchantments—are the ultimate source of raw material for writing. It is designed to take you from a single messy observation to an impactful piece of fiction. We will skip the endless theory and dive straight into the craft: mapping your city, executing structural revision sprints, and breaking down exactly where to send your work to get published.

 

Here are the details:

Date: 26th and 27th September 2026, (Saturday & Sunday)

Time: 11 AM - 2 PM

Venue: Champaca Bookstore, Vasanth Nagar

Workshop fee: Rs 5000/- per person. 

Key Takeaways:

  • The Art of Flash-Fiction: How to start small and write impactful stories in fragments.

  • Guided Practice: Participate in real-time writing and revision sprints alongside fellow writers.

  • Curated Reading: Engage with exceptional examples of city-focused literature.

  • In-person Mentorship: Receive feedback and tailored reading recommendations.

  • Submission-ready Work: Leave the workshop with a highly polished, well developed piece of flash fiction.

  • Publishing Roadmap: Learn exactly where and how to submit your work to literary journals.

Who is this workshop for?

If you want to begin, if you have begun, or are someone who wants to begin, again. This extensive writing workshop is open to all (including writers of other genres, as everyone can benefit from the practice of writing flash fiction).

About the facilitator: 

Apoorva Saini is a writer, editor, and translator based in Bangalore. She is the co-founder of Cities in Fiction, a digital public archive for locating real-world places in South Asian literature. She also runs The Bilingual Window, an online lit mag for original and translated short stories. Apoorva has studied creative writing from University of Edinburgh, Scotland, and Ambedkar University, Delhi.
